rationale: C21 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both are short presidential letters responding to Atomic Energy Commission-related findings, commending valuable service, expressing gratification at the Commission's accomplishments, and closing with confidence or praise arising from those accomplishments. The shared phraseology and progression are substantially more distinctive than mere atomic-energy subject overlap. C22 has a similar report–public-service–gratitude structure, while C03 shares the atomic-energy setting but not the child's commendatory structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The members of the Panel have performed a valuable public service and deserve the sincere thanks of the Government.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Chairman and members of the Commission join me in congratulations to you on the work of Joint Task Force Seven... Please convey... my commendation for a job well done.
shared_material.explanation: Both letters prominently commend participants whose work supported the Atomic Energy Commission.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The confirmation by the Panel that there is reason for pride in the Commission's accomplishments to date is a source of gratification to me
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I know you share my feelings of gratification at the accomplishments of the Commission's Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory
shared_material.explanation: The unusually close pairing of 'gratification' with the Commission's 'accomplishments' is distinctive shared language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am very much obliged for your letter... forwarding a copy of the Report
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Atomic Energy Commission has reported to me on the results of the tests
shared_material.explanation: Each begins from the receipt of findings and uses them as the basis for commendation and an affirmative assessment of Commission work.
